utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Before the witness is brought in, one small matter, and that is that just before we broke a photograph was put into evidence as P098.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It was put in under seal, though I didn't request it and it need not be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When that comes up, that will be unsealed, if that's an adequate description of the process. Is that all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's all. We're ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So we can bring in the witness then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If I could remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Now, Mr. Whiting has some more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we proceed, I think the screens need to be put up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness L-96. We are, I'll remind you, still in open session and so I'd just ask you to take care on not using your name. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, before we stopped yesterday, you had described for us witnessing the beating of Shaban Hoti on the first full night when you were at Lapusnik. Do you remember telling us about that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Witness, after that night did you on a night following that night see anything happen to Shaban Hoti?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before the second night, something else happened during the day. So before Shaban Hoti was beaten for the second time, something else happened during the day. If you're now asking me about the second night, the group consisting of the persons from the first night, at least it resembled that the group that was there during the first night, I think that they arrived just before midnight. I didn't have a watch, so I cannot say what exactly the time was. So they entered the room where Shaban Hoti was, and they beat him again. So as far as we could see from our room, they beat him really badly. They were jumping on him. When they finished with Shaban Hoti, they came back to our room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, before we get to that, I'm going to ask you a few questions about what you saw regarding that second beating. You said that the soldiers resembled the soldiers who had come in the first group. This second time, could you tell us approximately how many soldiers you saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the second time, there were five or six. I can't say whether this figure is the exact one, but at least there were five or six.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you remember what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing KLA uniforms, military uniforms, camouflaged. The KLA emblem could be seen on some of them because it was dark. One of them was carrying a torch light in his hand. So from this light what you could see is that there were five or six persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And, L-96, when you say that they went into the room where Shaban Hoti was, was that the second room on the upper floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the second room on the upper floor where Shaban Hoti was. And myself and the friends who were with me were in the first room. But in order to get into the second room, you had to go through our room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you describe what you saw in terms of the beating that occurred on this second occasion. What do you remember seeing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the second time I remember that they entered the room where Shaban Hoti was. I saw people stepping on Shaban Hoti, jumping on him, cursing him, shouting at him. That's what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You say they were shouting at him. Do you remember what they were shouting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were asking him, Will you ever come to KLA zones to translate? We will kill you. So very harsh words.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And could you see, was Shaban Hoti standing while this was happening or was he lying on the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shaban Hoti was lying down. He was very tired. He couldn't stand. His hands and feet were tied, and you had no idea whether he was alive or dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Witness, after the second beating, what happened? What's the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next thing that happened after the second beating is that these persons came to our room. One of them was holding the torch light and was looking at us on our faces. This person addressed (redacted) He -- with his torch light, he came to (redacted)’s face. And a person who was standing behind the person with a torch light, I don't know who he was exactly, but he told, No, Commander, this is not the person; this is the person. And then the person with the torch light directed the torch on my face and said to me, We will beat you to a pulp. And when he said that, We will beat you to a pulp, I realised that there was someone else that I knew there as well. I realised that there was not only one person in question, but there were at least two.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: L-96, we're now back in public session. You said that this person who had the flashlight had been addressed as commander. Did you -- were you able to see this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not there because the flashlight was directed on my eyes, so you couldn't see. I couldn't see any face, I couldn't see who it was, I couldn't even see the other persons who were with him because of the dazzling light.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: After this person who had the flashlight said this to you, what did he and the other soldiers do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night this was what was said to me, nothing else. Just shortly after they said this, they left, the door was locked, and nothing else -- nothing special happened that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, after the soldiers left, did they -- the door between the room you were in and the room that Shaban Hoti was in, was it closed or was it left open?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had left the door open. The door was at all times while I was there was open. During the day you could see Shaban Hoti lying with his hands and feet tied, so you couldn't tell whether he was alive or dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was he able to move at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were there and while we could see him, personally I never saw him move.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did he make any sounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. During that time, during my stay there, I never heard him speak, I never heard him shout. I heard nothing coming from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you said that before the night of the second beating of Shaban Hoti something occurred during the day. Can you tell us what it is that occurred during the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day - I don't know the exact time, whether it was noon or afternoon - Shala opened the door and brought Musli Belince inside. I knew Musli Belince from before; he's a very old person. He had in his arm a bag with medicine because he was using medicine at that time. So as soon as they opened the door, they just threw him in the room and he rolled several times on the floor. They started beating him with a wooden stick which was about 1 metre long, and they brought him to the room where Shaban Hoti was. Shaban -- Musli Belince could not stand on his feet. This happened during the day, so before the second night when the group came to Shaban Hoti's room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: L-96, who beat this man with a stick, could you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shala.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the stick, can you describe the stick, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about 1 metre long, like a piece of wood from the woods. It had -- it resembled a wood that grows in the mountains, like a branch, a thicker branch. So this is the piece of wood that Shala used to beat Belince.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And could you see where on his body he beat him with the stick?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Musli Belince was lying on the floor. We call him Mus. His short name was Mus. He would hit him on his feet, on his body. You couldn't tell whether he was alive or dead. He was ill anyways, even when he wasn't in the situation he was using medicine. I don't know what he was suffering from, but he was using medicine. This is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And, Witness, did -- can you describe how he hit him with the stick? Were they hard blows? Was he hitting him -- can you try to describe it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Shala grabbed the wood with both his hands. So we call it in Albanian a wooden stick. And he hit him on his feet, on his back, as hard as he could. Musli Belince was lying on the carpet and with his belly down, so his back was exposed. This is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did the beating occur in the room you were in or in the room that Shaban Hoti was in or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as he opened the door in our room, he just threw him inside, threw him on the floor, and he started beating him there in our room. And as far as I remember, he dragged him to the second room. And then he placed him in the room where Shaban Hoti was. The door remained open. It wasn't any other person in the room except for Shala. So he continued to beat Mus Belince in the room where Shaban Hoti was. This was it. In the end when he finished beating him, he returned him to our room. Musli Belince could not sit like normal people do, so he couldn't sit -- of course not on a chair because there were no chairs, but he couldn't sit on the floor. He wasn't fit to sit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you told us yesterday about somebody by the name of Muje Muslia from Belince. Is there any relationship between Muje Muslia and the man you've just been talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muje Musliu was Mus's son. He was son of Mus Musliu, because we use Mus for Musliu, Mus Belince. So Muje was his son.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So this man who was beaten was referred to both as Muje Belince and Muje Musliu?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The man who was beaten, his name was Mus Belince. His last name was Musliu. And Muje who you mentioned was the son of this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And is Belince the village that he is from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Belince is a village situated between Shtime and Carraleve. It's about 3 kilometres from Shtime, 1 kilometre from Racak. It's not a very big village. It's a small village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And, Witness, is this the village that this man who was being beaten was from, Belince?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was from the village of Belince, Mus Musliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Shala say anything while he was beating this man, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't say a word, he just beat him. And he looked like a mad person, like a savage person. And he was looking at us while he was beating Mus. We were scared to death. When someone can beat such an old person, what can someone say about us who were much younger?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask you some questions about another topic now. I'm going to bring you to the next day, the day following the second beating of Shaban Hoti. Do you follow me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did something happen on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second day after Shaban Hoti was beaten, is this what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about the day after -- the day after the second beating of Shaban Hoti.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Shaban Hoti was beaten, it was midnight, we were still there. Someone was sleeping, someone was awake. The morning arrived. It was a usual morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that day, did anything happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Something very important for me happened that day. Isak Musliu came to the door that day. Behind him was a soldier with a Kalashnikov. I didn't know who he was. Behind him was Murrizi. They passed through the room and went to where Shaban Hoti was. As the three of them entered the next room, after a short time, I would say one or two minutes, Murrizi mentioned my name. He said, Hey you, come here. He mentioned my name. So I got up on my feet and went to them. When I entered the room, he told me -- he ordered me to stand next to the wall. Isak Musliu said to Murriz, Tie his hands up with a chain. Murrizi was following Isak Musliu's orders, so he chained both my hands up, as I'm showing at the moment. After they chained me up, the soldier wearing a uniform and with a Kalashnikov, he was in a state of readiness. I was scared to death. Because when you see someone like that, you know that death might be close. He started to slap me hard on the face. I fell on my knees. When I was on my knees, Isak Musliu made a karate move and hit me and it was a really hard blow, and I fell on the ground with my hands tied. When I was on the ground, I know very well that he started kicking me without any control on himself. I know that for a short time I lost consciousness because of the beating. So when he hit me like that, he stopped. Then he said to Murriz again, Make him stand up. He -- Murrizi grabbed me by the hand and helped me to stand up. Isak told Murrizi to blindfold me. Murrizi found a towel somewhere. This towel was in the room. So he blindfolded me with a towel. I couldn't see anything else there. I know that Murrizi grabbed me by my two hands. I know that the chain was about half a metre long, and then Murrizi was dragging me. I know that he was dragging me towards the first room, and then he was dragging me down the staircase. I had no idea where he was taking me because I was blindfolded. He was just dragging the chain. When he removed the blindfold, I saw -- I realised where I was standing. As I turned my head, I saw Isak Musliu and Murrizi asked Isak Musliu, Where shall I put him? He told him, Put him in the first room, not in the other, (redacted). I didn't know who was where, but he told Murrizi, Put him in the other room, not where (redacted) (redacted). So Murrizi opened the door, put me inside, and he locked the door. It was a door made of metal. So now I was in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, you said that when the blindfold was taken off you could see where you were. Where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- if you have the picture, I can show you exactly where I was. I was opposite the metal door on the way to the toilet, in the same yard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you need a redaction, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There's a reference to a relative there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could switch the monitor to Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, can you see on the screen an image, and it's -- for purposes of the record, it's the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's the image on page 11 of P006, and this is an image -- we're looking at P005. Witness, do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this image very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what is this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the door where Murrizi stopped me, where he removed the blindfold. So from the second room to this location, I was blindfolded and I didn't know where I was heading to. But on this point, he removed the un -- blindfold. So when I turned my head, I saw Isak Musliu, he was somewhere in the yard. He -- Murrizi then addressed Isak Musliu and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. asked him, Where shall I put him? He said, Put him in the first room, not in the other room, because (redacted) is there. I didn't know that there was a second room. I just knew that there was a toilet there because we used that toilet. So Murrizi opened the door, placed me inside, and then locked the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We can take that image off now. And, Your Honour, if we could have another redaction. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, can you describe, please, for us the room that you were placed into.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The room had a low ceiling. It was about 3 metres -- 2 and a half to 3 metres long. The floor was made of -- it was a concrete floor. There was hay on the floor. Behind the door there was a bucket, a plastic bucket, that was used for -- as a toilet. There were two shelves. It looked like a stable. Litter, hay, you could even see blood. It had a window next to the door; we could see it on the image. So this is my description of the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you stay in this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I spent four days and four nights in this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you tell us what the temperature was in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The temperature and the smell cannot describe -- be described. There are no words that can describe them. It was July, midsummer. Nobody could stand the smell.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, did you -- were there other people in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I entered the room, I saw I think around six persons, but what is interesting as a fact is that I knew everyone who was in that room. They were all from our municipality. From their appearance I can say that I knew some better than the others. I don't know exactly which villages they came from, but basically I knew all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell us who these people were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first one lying next to the window was Emin Emini from Carraleve village; I knew him from before the war. Next to Emin Emini were two other persons from Carraleve; they were from Xhemtafa family. I didn't know their exact names. I had seen them before -- before the war on the markets. I didn't know their first name, but their family name was Xhemtafa. In the line, so after these two persons, was Hyzri Belince; he used to sell limestone before the war. After Hyzri was Luta. He used to be a forest ranger. I knew him before the war as well. As far as I remember next to Luta was Bashkim, I think that was his name. I had seen him in Shtime a couple of times before, but I don't know exactly whether he was from Shtime or the Shtime district. After him was Adem Godance, and after Adem Godance was (redacted) (redacted) who used to work as an electrician; he had been an electrician for 20 years. (redacted) (redacted) After (redacted) was me, myself. So there were no others on that day in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, you referred to a Hyzri Belince. Is that a person by the name of Hyzri who is from Belince or is Belince the family name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hyzri is from Belince village, of the same village that Muje and Muslia are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you know the family name of Hyzri?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his family name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you also referred to Adem Godance. Is that somebody -- again, same question: Is he from Godance or is that -- or is Godance his family name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned Adem, saying that I didn't know his family name. I know only that he was from Godance. That's what I said Adem from Godance. I didn't know for sure. Even now I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, with the assistance of the usher I'm going to give you a blank piece of paper and a pen. And I'm going to ask you, please, to draw the room for us, and if we could put it on the ELMO. And can you show -- draw the room and then show where these people were lying and show us the door and the window and the bucket.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the door. This is where the window was. The bucket, the plastic bucket, was here. Here lying was Emin Emini. Next to him, the two from Xhemtafa family. After those two from Xhemtafa family came Hyzri. After Hyzri was Luta. After Luta was Bashkim. Next to him was Adem. Next to Adem was (redacted) I -- I couldn't fit in in the corner; there was no room. So I was staying here because there was no more room to lie there at the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just ask that the record reflect that on the picture that's been drawn by the witness, on the side of the box that has the circle, square, and another square, the witness identified the circle as being the plastic bucket, the square to the right of that circle as being the door, and the square to the right of that, which he has just put an X in, as being the window. The lines that are drawn along the side that is perpendicular to that line are -- he has identified as people -- individuals who are lying on the floor. And he has identified who they are, starting from the line that is closest to the box with the X in it. And then the final line, which is by itself on the opposite -- on the line -- on the wall that is opposite to the door, he has identified as himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, did another -- after that first day, did there come a time when another prisoner came into the room or was, shall we say, brought into the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the next day they brought Shaban Hoti there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you remember where he was placed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the same room. There was only one place, across the window, for someone to lie, between the window and me. This is where Shaban Hoti was lying on the next day. Because there was no more room here. When he came in, Shaban Hoti, he stood here. There was an empty place where; whereas, the bucket, as I said, was in this corner here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, how many windows were in that room, just to be clear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one window here. There was also steel mesh above the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that the record reflect that the witness has drawn a line and identified that place as being the place where Shaban Hoti was and he has put a line identifying himself. And I would ask that this paper be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P99.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if we could switch from the ELMO to the Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, can you see that image again in front of you, the same one you saw before?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And for the record, the image that we're showing is from P005, and it's the same image from page 11 of P006. I'm going to ask Mr. Younis to bring us inside of that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the inside of that room? We'll do that again. This is the outside of the room that you had seen before. And now we'll go inside the room, which is identified as storage room A5. L-96, do you recognise the inside of that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where I stood shut up for four days and nights, in this very place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is this the room that you were just -- that you just drew a picture of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the room I just draw. I remember very, very well that this is where we were kept prisoners, myself and the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You can take the image off.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, can you describe the physical condition of the other prisoners in the room, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The physical condition of the prisoners in that room was bad. Two of those, those from Carraleve, Xhemtafa family, were in worse condition; they looked traumatised. They never uttered a word. We couldn't tell whether they were sleeping, awake. Sometimes they drank some water. I saw them drinking, but they were lying there just inert. After that worse was -- for the moment was Shaban Hoti after that. He too was completely passed out I would say. Then came Lut Shomari [phoen], this is how we called him, or Luta Ahbete [phoen]. He was the forest ranger I said earlier. He, too, was -- I saw it with my own eyes when he was peeing in that bucket, he was peeing blood. Personally, I felt very bad. Shefqet Godance seemed to be in a better condition. Adem, he didn't look very bad either. Bashkim, so, so. And Hyzri also so so. And Emin Emini was in a very bad state. He said, I have been here for 55 days. This is what I heard him say, this word, I've been here for 55 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, you may have already said this, but Luta, the forest ranger, do you know what village he was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Luta was from Crni Breg village. I know it very well that he was from that village. He worked (redacted) as a forest ranger.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: After you were placed in that room, did you see Shala again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him several times during the time I was in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you explain to us how you would see him? What would happen that would cause you to see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think once or twice after I went down he brought us bread. Shala and Murrizi were the ones who brought it to us. Then one evening it was a little before dusk, one of the prisoners, I think it was Shefqet Godance, asked Shala to go out because the stench was horrible and we couldn't stand it. It was very hot. He asked Shala -- he kindly asked him to take us out in the open air for some minutes. Then Shala let us go out to the door. There, around the door you can see the place. Shala was standing there beside us with his Kalashnikov. We were sitting down to breathe some fresh air. Without asking him, he said to us of his own free will, Don't worry, 60 people have left -- six people have left -- 60 people have died -- died in this prison. Then after some minutes, after ten minutes, he made us go in -- back inside. After us I asked Shefqet Ramadani --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to interrupt you for a moment. I'm going to ask you to repeat what it was that Shala said, because there was a little difficulty with the translation. Just so it's clear, can you repeat what it is that Shala said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were at the door, Shala knew that we were sad, that we're afraid. Without ask -- any one of us asking us, we didn't want to ask him any questions. He said, Don't worry too much, you who are prisoners here, because from this prison so far 60 people have died. This is what he said to us. And that was the end of it. He asked us to go inside. He closed the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you said that -- you said that sometimes Shala and Murrizi would bring you food in this room. During the four days that you were there, did you get food every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The first day I was taken there I know they gave us to eat. During the second day, I know they brought us water. And during the last two days, I think it was two days or maybe more, I don't remember well, they didn't give us anything to eat and nothing to drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When they brought water, can you describe how they would give you the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they brought us the water in plastic bottles of 1 litre and a half. They brought us three, four such bottles, just threw us them there on the floor. Every one of us got a bottle or two people shared a bottle; it depended. This is how they gave us the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, did you -- during those four days did you talk to any of the other prisoners in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I have, mostly with (redacted) from Godance because he was a friend. Even today he's a friend of mine. And I felt closer to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And he was --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...spoke also with Lut.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry. And also with who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Bashkim, with Lut who said some words. But mostly as I said, I talked with (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And (redacted) was lying next to you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was lying next to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you able to talk freely in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Shala was not there, yes; when he was there, none of us dared utter a word. Shala always told us not to talk with each other, not to say anything. But some time passed, he went out, and we could exchange some words. We did speak to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did Shala give you any other instructions or orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Each time he came, he told us not to go to the window and look out to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, (redacted) did he tell you how long he had been in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said, I've been here for 22 days when I went there. When I was -- went there, he told me, I've been here for 22 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did he tell you how he had been brought to the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't discuss this. No, we didn't discuss that. I remember this. We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything about other prisoners who had been there before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I want to know whether we are in closed session or in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We are in open session, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you what (redacted) told me, only I want it to be in closed session if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we go into private session please, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We're now back in public session -- open session. Did you talk with Shaban Hoti after he was brought into the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you remember what he told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For example, at that time Shaban Hoti for us was an unknown person; we didn't know him. According to his words he was from Pristina. I didn't know at that time where he came from. He started to say that -- to explain how he was taken and brought there. He said that he was a professor. He told us that his economic situation at home was very poor. He told us that some Russian journalists had asked for a translator that could speak Russian and Albanian and who could work with them as a translator. So Shaban had met them, and they asked him to work with him in war zones to carry out some interviews with some KLA personnel commanders. So Shaban told me that they gave him 50 Deutschmarks so that he could go and translate with him -- with them, so translate from Russian into Albanian and from Albanian into Russian. And he then said -- he didn't mention the zone exactly where, but said that he was captured by the KLA while working with the Russian journalists. This is what I heard from Shaban Hoti.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And, Witness, you told us yesterday that you had also heard information about Shaban Hoti from Shala. Had you -- had Shala already told you that information? Was that before you talked to Shaban Hoti himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first room, in the room where we were for the first time, Shala said, Look, a person who goes to translate for the Russians, look what will happen to him. But he didn't say anything about Shaban going and translating for the journalists or where he was captured or that he took 50 Deutschmarks. He just said, Look who will happen to a person who translates for the Russians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's a little early for the break, but it's a convenient time. I'm happy to press on, but if the Court wishes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think another quarter hour, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to move to another subject, Witness, and that is the last day you were in that room at the end of the four days. Can you tell us what happened after -- at the end of four days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the last day, Shala came and opened the door and said to us, Now you will all go outside. The one who will make any attempt to run, I will kill him on the spot. He opened the door --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, could you see what kind of weapon Shala had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shala had a Kalashnikov without a wooden butt. Murrizi had an M-48.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you said that Shyqyri - and I'm probably pronouncing the name wrong - had to be carried by you and some others. Do you remember who carried him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Shyqa in the beginning when we got out of the gate, Milaim Hoxha was carrying him; he was from Racak. After Milaim, we took it in turns. Bashkim, Adem, myself, we all took it in turns for as long as we could carry him. And Shala ordered us -- if he ordered us not to take a turn, then we wouldn't. (redacted) -- I did not see him carry him. There were some elderly people who could not even carry themselves, walk themselves, let alone carry Shyqa. That's how we walked on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, what time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was I think about 10.00 or 11.00 in the morning, an hour or an hour and a half, something like that. It was very hot, a very hot day. We had not eaten anything or drunk anything. It was very hot. This is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, we walked up the mountain, always escorted by Murrizi at the front, Shala at the back, the last one. And we came up to a major road. It was in fact a path, a major path, in the forest. And we went towards Berisa, in the direction of Berisa, towards Kuriz [phoen]. I remember there was a path that crossed there our path, and there we saw some persons in a tractor -- on a tractor, civilians armed, and they were coming towards us. I was the last one, close to Shala, and this was a kind of a clearing in the forest. And there I heard Shala say, Commander Celiku is coming and I'll ask -- I'll ask him what I'm supposed to do with you. These people in uniform were probably 20 or 30 metres, they were coming away from us. They were coming in the opposite direction, from the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened after Shala said, Commander Celiku is coming and I'll ask him what I'm supposed to do? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shala told us immediately to stop where we were, and they all fell on the ground, (redacted) -- they just dropped there because they couldn't stand on their feet. Shala went 7 or 8 metres away, and the commander who was coming, they got together. They were talking, but I couldn't hear what they were saying. They were 7 or 8 metres away from us. They spoke to each other very briefly, but what they said I don't know. Shala came to us and a soldier came together with Shala. He was one of the people who was with the commander. Shala came and ordered us to get up on our feet, and we continued our march. Murrizi was at the front of the line; Shala the last one. And this soldier that was given by the commander to Shala, he was walking up and down the line. He did not stay exactly at the end of the line; he sometimes went to the middle or the front of the line. And we went up the mountain. So there was another soldier in addition to Shala and Murrizi. We never knew his name. We never heard a pseudonym or a name. This is what happened that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, the commander that Shala spoke to 7 or 8 metres away from you, were you able to get a clear view of this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw his face very well. He did not have a hat. He was in uniform, one colour uniform. He had a belt. We called it "opasac." It was -- I saw a black satchel or bag across his soldier. And after the conversation was over, he went down, went to the other soldiers, and other -- there was some civilians who were armed -- there were some people on the tractor, but he went to those people who were out of the tractor, whereas us, together with Shala and Murrizi and the soldier that was given by this commander to Shala, we continued on our way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: L-96, do you -- were you able to tell approximately how old this commander was that Shala spoke with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person that day looked young. He was not shaved, maybe an unshaven beard for two or three weeks. He looked hollow, he had hollow cheeks; black -- dark hair, but there was a lot of dust in the air that day; tall. This is how he looked that day -- what he looked to me that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you said he was an unshaven beard for two or three weeks. Is that what you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It looked like that, that he had two weeks -- he had gone two weeks without shaving. He looked like he had not shaved. I thought maybe two weeks -- probably three.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how long approximately did Shala and this person speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, five minutes at the most. Shala came back, and when he came back he had a soldier with him. Five minutes approximately. We were all sitting down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, you've already told us about being interviewed in February of 2002 by UNMIK. During that interview were photographs shown to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you remember how they were shown to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the interview was a long one with the investigators, the UNMIK investigators. When the interview was over, the investigator told me that now the interview is over and you have to look at these pictures. He explained to me, There will be six pictures on a piece of paper. Each photograph has a number on it. You have to round the number of the person that you recognise, and when you circle the number you have to write your name beside the circle. And I said, Yes, I understand. There was this piece of paper with six photographs. He asked me, Do you know any one of these people here? At the moment, if I speak the truth, I saw Shala, and I banged my fist on the table and I said, This is the one. And he said, Don't hurry, you can have -- you can look at him for five minutes, ten minutes. You can go outside, calm yourself down. And I said, I don't need to go outside. And I underlined the number with a pen and I wrote here (redacted) and I wrote here, this is Haradin Bala, Shala. This was the first one. The second --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you for a moment, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could show -- with the assistance of the usher if we could show tab 7, please. And I would ask that it not be placed on the ELMO. Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, we're back into open session. You -- before we looked at the photographs, you described how this encounter with this commander who is referred to as Commander Celiku and then continuing the march with a third soldier. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went up the path, and after some time Murrizi, as I said, he was always at the front of the line. And I heard Murrizi once say, Where are we going, to Berisa or Klecka? Shala did not answer. He did not say Berisa or Klecka; he just said, Take a left. After a little bit of time, there was a path there on the left and Murrizi took the left path. We had to follow him, Murrizi. From there, maybe a thousand metres from there, there was a clearing, a meadow, and there was a cherry tree there and also a well, a spring of water. It was a spring -- a source of water. At the cherry tree, Shala ordered us to stop there and we all sat down. We were so tired, exhausted. It was very hot. Shala, Murrizi, and the third soldier - I don't know his name to this day - they sat down there with their Kalashnikovs in their hands. Shala and the other soldier had a Kalashnikov, while Murrizi had a rifle. We stopped there, had a break for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to ask the usher to show you image 7 from P001. Witness, have you seen this map before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did I show it to you when we were preparing your testimony before coming here to court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was like that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you orient yourself on this map? Do you see where it's marked Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I turn it like this? Yes. I will circle Lapusnik here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Actually, what I'm going to ask you is if -- are you able to draw approximately the route that you think you took from Lapusnik to the cherry tree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the red circle is, that's where Lapusnik is and the prison. This is the route from the prison to the cherry tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, are you able to show approximately where the encounter with the commander occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me turn it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if -- is that circle where you -- where approximately the encounter where the commander occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here the encounter with the commander and the persons who are with him took place, and here's where he assigned Shala another soldier. Up to this point, we walked only with Shala and Murrizi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, could you put a number 1 next to that circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the point where Murrizi asked, Are we going to Berisa or are we going to Klecka, and Shala said, Turn left, are you able -- can you put a 2 there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P106.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, how long did you spend at the cherry tree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we stayed two to three hours at the cherry tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, after the two or three hours at the cherry tree, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After some time, Shala received his lunch. We were watching while he was eating in our presence. When he finished his lunch, he lit a cigarette, because he smoked then, and then he stood up. And he said, Now I will call out some names, and he who hears his name shall come here and separate from the group. He took out a notebook from his pocket, a pen, and he started to call names. I heard him when he said (redacted) (redacted) then the person should reply, Yes, I'm here, and then go to the other side, separate from the group. I heard him call the name of Adem. I heard him call the names of the Xhemtafa family members; there were three of them there. I know that the person from Varigovc also left with the first group. So he gathered them and said to them, Listen, I will take you to another point. He said to Murriz, You will stay here and be careful; he said the same thing to the other person whose name I didn't know. So Shala set off with this group, and they walked downhill.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, you said he called out (redacted), Adem, the three Xhemtafas, and the person from Varigovc. Do you remember any other of the prisoners leaving with this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Milaim Hoxha was also in this group, Milaim Hoxha from Racak. Muje from Belince.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, you said that Shala ate lunch. Do you remember how he got a lunch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone from uphill, from Berisa, brought him lunch. I don't know who it was; I just saw that it was a man who brought him the food. We just saw him eat there in our presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did this person bring food for anybody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite interesting, the fact I mean that neither Murrizi or the other soldier had lunch with Shala, and let alone us prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that Shala left with this group. Did he -- did Shala return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After some time Shala returned. I could say that about 40 minutes had passed; it was more than half an hour that had passed when he returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, after Shala called out the names of this other -- this second group, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shala said, Now we will go to another point. He ordered Murriz to lead the group again. In the beginning, we took the same direction as the first group; and after 2 to 300 metres he then said to Murriz to take the right. It was a young forest there; it was like a mountain path, not a path used by tractors. So it was kind of a clearing. We were down -- going downhill. And there nearby was a forest. We got to a main road, if I can say so, a road that can be used by tractors as well. There we crossed a small stream, and Shala stopped there and said to us that we could drink some water. Some had some water; some didn't. Then there was a meadow on a turn, and then we reached a junction, a crossroads. Just before the crossroads, Shala said to Murrizi, Find a path that can take us to the mountain. Murrizi kept to the left. We carried on for another 100 metres on the left side. And then Shala saw a path used by Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. pedestrians, which we followed for another 100 metres. There was a clearing. Someone had can you tell the woods there, so it was a clearing. And Shala said that we should stop there. We all stopped there. As we were lined up, he ordered us to sit and we sat. I was the last.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go briefly into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, what happened after you all sat down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we sat down, Shala, Murrizi, and the soldier all were at 7 metres away from us. Shala then furthered for another 5 metres. There I saw Shala as he turned. He put a phone, a cellphone, in the pocket. I don't know whether he spoke to someone, but I saw him put the phone in his pocket. Then he came to Murrizi and to the soldier. He spoke with them. I don't know what he told them. They took up positions. Shala was in the middle, Murrizi to his left, the soldier to his right. So Shala was in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then unexpectedly Shala said, This is your death penalty. When he said, This is your death sentence, I saw him charge his Kalashnikov, both Shala and the soldier who was opposite to me and Murrizi as well. In that moment I just screamed, No. And as I was crouching, my hand was (redacted). I couldn't escape in their direction, but I could just run on the opposite direction. I was just about 1 metre away (redacted) when I heard burst of fire coming from two Kalashnikovs. The burst was directed on the people who were sitting down. I remember that when I turned my head, the person who was shooting in my direction was trying to get -- as I was running, I was just falling down and standing up. And I just rolled down the road for 200 metres. There I stopped. I couldn't proceed because then it was kind of uphill and I thought that I could be visible to them and they would shoot me. There I found two stones and said to myself, In case they come and catch me, I will use these for my defence. I could no longer hear any bursts of fire, any scream, any sound, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent quite a long time there. I had to follow the situation to see what was going to happen. It was clear to me that I left (redacted) (redacted). I walked down the hill. It was somewhere between Kishna Reka and Nekovce. I had to wait till it got dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what language was the interview in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interview was conducted in English and Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember the next time you were interviewed by CCIU?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was exactly a year later in 2001, it was August.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And before that interview, did you go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before going to CCIU in Pristina in August, with (redacted) and (redacted) we went to Lapusnik, to the prison. From Lapusnik by car - I had bought a four-wheel drive at the time - we went to that rock where we saw Commander Celiku. From that cross path, we went to the cherry tree. We left the car there. And I explained to them, That's where we came all together and where the two groups were divided. And now we have to find where the killed people are. It took some time to find the place where they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eventually I found where -- the place where they were executed, and they had put some soil on it. They had covered them but, you know, the animals had passed there and there had been snow and the weather conditions. And some of the bones showed. And I told (redacted) (redacted), This is where I was. (redacted) This is where (redacted) was. This is where I was crouching and my hand was on (redacted) shoulder. And there were skulls there and bones there. And (redacted) lost control and said, I will not go home without his body. I want his body. Then we took him by the arms. We had to stop him because he lost control completely. He could not control himself at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, did you -- when you were interviewed then by CCIU, did you tell them where this place was where you saw these bones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went to CCIU in Pristina now, not in Lipjan, and I told them how I had been to the prison, I went to the place of execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you take them to the place of execution and show them where it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I took them there to the place of execution and I told them that, If you leave these victims here tonight, tomorrow there will be no bones here for you to find.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think this is a convenient time to break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting. We will adjourn now overnight, resuming tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, there's just one small matter, that is I think there is one redaction from this last bit. I thank the registrar for alerting me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 26th day of January, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24 25
